findings.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion when the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls it with the admin fine-grained authz feature enabled
canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, causing internal 500 errors instead of permission decisions in the token-exchange flow
getEvaluationContext is a dead private method with its unused imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext, and unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import)

Inconsistent conventions between hasPermission(ClientModel, String) and hasPermission(String) for locating the 'all clients' type resource: one auto-creates via schema, the other fails closed with a raw findByName

setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent branch calls it on every client deletion under V2, causing client deletion to fail with a 500
Per-client authorization resources created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never deleted when a client is removed under V2, leaving orphaned resource rows

PermissionClientTest only deletes a client in testManageAllClients using the resource-server admin client, so the V2 realmAdminClient deletion path with permission resources present is never exercised
The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and canMapClientScopeRoles evaluator have zero test coverage (no positive or negative tests for client-scope-level role-mapping)

canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing admin token exchange paths consulting them to return a 500 instead of a 403, with no feature-detection fallback at call sites

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) passes the result of getResourceTypeResource to findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE/500 when the type-level Clients resource doesn't exist in fresh realms

Wrapping the cleanup listener in registerListener with a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check silently stops V1 permission resource cleanup when the flag is disabled, causing orphaned authz resources to accumulate

In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), a type-level all-clients permission is ignored when a per-client resource exists, making behavior depend on whether a per-client resource was materialized; no test covers this combination

AdminPermissions.java registerListener: wrapping event listener handler in ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check disables cleanup of authorization resources for removed clients/roles/groups when the feature is disabled, leaking persisted resources

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a boolean decision, causing 500 errors instead of 403 for legitimate token-exchange API calls
ClientPermissionsV2.getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code since its only caller canExchangeTo unconditionally throws; should be deleted or wired in

ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel) only checks global MANAGE_CLIENTS or type-level MANAGE permission, dropping per-object permission evaluation and contradicting the documented interface contract

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback can pass a null resource into getPolicyStore().findByResource, causing NPE/500 on first evaluation when the type resource was never created
ClientRemovedEvent listener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 implements by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, causing client deletion to fail with a 500
canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a permission decision, surfacing as a 500 rather than 403 or proper not-supported response
getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource, creating an N+1 evaluation loop on the admin client-list path
AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient accepting both internal id and clientId creates a cross-namespace collision where a permission granted for client A can silently authorize client B
hasPermission passes a possibly null type-level resource to findByResource, producing an NPE or empty-policy 500 rather than a clean deny

canView/canManageClientScopes/canManage collapse all client-scope decisions to the realm-wide all-clients resource, silently changing per-object semantics with no versioning or interface contract update

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the V1 client-deletion cleanup contract that AdminPermissions.registerListener depends on — client removal fails or orphans authz resources in V2 realms
ClientPermissionsV2 canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange authorization in V2 realms (500 errors instead of grant/deny decisions)

ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, resource, getPermissions, and isPermissionsEnabled — breaking the admin console per-client Permissions tab and AdminPermissionsEvaluator REST API

AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which may disable role/group/client removal cleanup in V2 realms if governed by a different feature flag, causing orphaned authz resource accumulation

ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel) overrides V1 semantics of MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role with 'role OR realm-wide Clients MANAGE permission', silently granting client-scope management to a different population than documented

All-clients fallback gate in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) tests the wrong permission population: findByResource misses resourceType-scoped permissions, so an all-clients grant fails per-client enforcement and admins get inconsistent 403s
V2 overrides canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role short-circuit that V1 applies, denying role mapping to admins with the manage-clients role

Per-client policy-management methods (mapRolesPermission, managePermission, setPermissionsEnabled, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, so a MANAGE-scoped admin has no bootstrapping path to create the permission that would unblock themselves, causing 500s

The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature-flag guard on event cleanup listeners is not the same switch that selects MgmtPermissionsV2, so if V2 is enabled while that flag is off, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers never run, accumulating orphaned Client resources and policies that leak deleted-client UUIDs and grow unboundedly

New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope in ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles has zero test coverage; the role-mapping test never imports or grants the scope, so the permission branch could regress unchecked
Positive-path assertions in PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient are 'doesn't throw' checks with no state verification (e.g. no listAll() confirming role assignment)
PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients passes a null representation to create() when asserting 403, so it doesn't verify authorization denial for a valid client

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener fails and per-client authorization Resource/scope-permission/policy rows are orphaned on client deletion under the V2 feature, potentially aborting client removal itself

AdminPermissions now wraps the entire role/client/group removal cleanup in a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check, so when the feature is disabled, previously-removed entities' permission resources are not cleaned up, leaving dangling rows that persist across disable-to-enable transitions

resolveClient/getOrCreateResource uses client ID or clientId as resource name in the same name column, creating ambiguity where a clientId string matching another client's UUID-shaped name, or a re-created client with a new internal ID, causes lookups to miss the per-client resource and fall through to the all-clients resource or silently lose permissions, with no migration handling re-created clients

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException when called from AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent branch in V2 mode, causing client deletion to fail with a 500 and orphaned authz resources/policies
ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false, causing a 500 instead of a denied (403) decision during token-exchange authorization in V2 realms
ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission NPEs when getResourceTypeResource returns null for the type-level all-clients resource, crashing canManage/canView on freshly-configured realms
hasGrantedPermission re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() without a null guard, risking NPE for future callers since the null check lives in the calling method getClientsWithPermission

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion when the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls it with the admin fine-grained authz feature enabled

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, a ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent triggers management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 now overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). If the enabled feature causes management(...) to use MgmtPermissionsV2/ClientPermissionsV2, the listener will throw during client removal, breaking client deletion/cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, causing internal 500 errors instead of permission decisions in the token-exchange flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` (and related permission builders like `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, etc.) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any runtime path (e.g., token-exchange) calls these methods when `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, it would result in an unhandled exception rather than a permission decision. However, the diff alone does not show that the token-exchange flow actually invokes `canExchangeTo` under V2, nor that it would surface as an HTTP 500; that part of the finding is not directly verifiable from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getEvaluationContext is a dead private method with its unused imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext, and unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import)
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags getEvaluationContext as a dead/unused private method (never called), which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment. It also notes related unused imports, but that’s additional detail, not a different issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent conventions between hasPermission(ClientModel, String) and hasPermission(String) for locating the 'all clients' type resource: one auto-creates via schema, the other fails closed with a raw findByName

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the inconsistency described: in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is missing it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` (which can create/ensure the "all clients" resource) before evaluating (`resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`). But `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String)` looks up the "all clients" resource only via `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` and returns `false` if it doesn't exist, without using the schema helper. This is a real, diff-grounded convention/robustness issue, though it’s not clearly a functional bug given that permissions for a missing resource likely can’t exist anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent branch calls it on every client deletion under V2, causing client deletion to fail with a 500

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Also in the diff, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now runs (guarded by `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`) and on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` it unconditionally calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. Separately, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return a cached `ClientPermissionsV2`. If `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` under the enabled feature (which is the apparent intent given the V2 additions), then deleting a client will trigger the listener and throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, causing a server error during client deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-client authorization resources created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never deleted when a client is removed under V2, leaving orphaned resource rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds CLIENTS as a new resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema and resolves client IDs in getOrCreateResource, enabling creation of per-client authorization resources (resource name/id == client id). Cleanup on client removal relies on AdminPermissions.registerListener calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent. Under V2, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) is explicitly unimplemented and throws UnsupportedOperationException. There is no alternative deletion/cleanup path in the diff, so per-client resources created via getOrCreateResource would not be deleted on client removal (and the listener may even fail), leaving orphaned resource rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PermissionClientTest only deletes a client in testManageAllClients using the resource-server admin client, so the V2 realmAdminClient deletion path with permission resources present is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients`, the client creation and deletion are both performed via `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients()...` (the managed realm admin client), not via the injected `ManagedClient client` (the admin-permissions resource-server client). The test also creates permission resources beforehand via `createAllPermission(client, clientsType, ...)`, so the realmAdminClient deletion path *is* exercised with permission resources present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and canMapClientScopeRoles evaluator have zero test coverage (no positive or negative tests for client-scope-level role-mapping)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and adds/implements `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client)` (see `ClientPermissionEvaluator` and `ClientPermissionsV2#canMapClientScopeRoles` which checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). In the added/updated tests (notably `PermissionClientTest`), there are positive/negative tests for `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, but none grant or assert behavior specifically for `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, nor any test exercising client-scope-level role mapping paths. So the finding about zero test coverage for this new scope/evaluator is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing admin token exchange paths consulting them to return a 500 instead of a 403, with no feature-detection fallback at call sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that in `ClientPermissionsV2` several token-exchange-related methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`) (and other permission-creation methods) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). However, the finding’s claim that “admin token exchange paths consult them” and therefore will return a 500 “with no feature-detection fallback at call sites” is not verifiable from this diff because no call sites or token-exchange flow changes are shown here. What is verifiable is the architectural risk introduced: if any existing code path invokes these methods under V2, it would result in an unhandled runtime exception (likely 500).

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) passes the result of getResourceTypeResource to findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE/500 when the type-level Clients resource doesn't exist in fresh realms

Wrapping the cleanup listener in registerListener with a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check silently stops V1 permission resource cleanup when the flag is disabled, causing orphaned authz resources to accumulate

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the entire cleanup logic for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously, `management(...).roles()/clients()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` would run regardless. With the feature flag disabled, the listener now performs no cleanup at all, so any existing permission resources/policies associated with removed roles/clients/groups would not be disabled/cleaned up, potentially leaving orphaned authz artifacts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), a type-level all-clients permission is ignored when a per-client resource exists, making behavior depend on whether a per-client resource was materialized; no test covers this combination

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code evaluates only one `Resource`: it uses the per-client resource if `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` returns non-null, and it falls back to the type-level "all clients" resource (`getResourceTypeResource(...CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) only when the per-client resource is missing. There is no path that evaluates both and unions scopes, so an existing per-client resource can effectively mask a granted type-level permission. The added tests cover "only one client" and "all clients" scenarios but do not cover the mixed case (both resources exist) to catch this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.java registerListener: wrapping event listener handler in ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check disables cleanup of authorization resources for removed clients/roles/groups when the feature is disabled, leaking persisted resources

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the PR wraps all event handling (`RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, `GroupRemovedEvent`) in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` was always invoked on those removal events. With this change, when the feature is disabled, those cleanup calls will not run at all, so any existing authz artifacts tied to removed roles/clients/groups would no longer be cleaned up via this listener.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a boolean decision, causing 500 errors instead of 403 for legitimate token-exchange API calls

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken)` and `exchangeToPermission(ClientModel)` are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` rather than returning a boolean/permission decision. If any runtime path invokes these methods (e.g., token-exchange authorization checks), this would surface as an unhandled runtime exception (likely HTTP 500) instead of a controlled denial (e.g., 403). The diff itself shows the exception-throwing behavior, though it does not show call sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code since its only caller canExchangeTo unconditionally throws; should be deleted or wired in

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, the private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is not referenced anywhere in the file. All token-exchange related overrides (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, etc.) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and no other method calls `getEvaluationContext`, so it is effectively dead code in this diff. This is not a runtime defect (Java allows unused private methods), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue that should be removed or wired in.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel) only checks global MANAGE_CLIENTS or type-level MANAGE permission, dropping per-object permission evaluation and contradicting the documented interface contract

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the `ClientPermissionEvaluator` contract for `canManage(ClientScopeModel clientScope)` explicitly documents only a global check: admin role `MANAGE_CLIENTS` and (for V2) permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (no per-object client-scope permission is described). `ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel)` delegates to `canManageClientScopes()`, which matches that documented behavior (checks `MANAGE_CLIENTS` or `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` at the type/all-clients level). The finding’s claim that this contradicts the interface contract and drops per-object evaluation is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback can pass a null resource into getPolicyStore().findByResource, causing NPE/500 on first evaluation when the type resource was never created

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), the fallback path does call policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without an explicit null-check after resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). However, the diff does not show getResourceTypeResource’s contract/implementation, and AdminPermissionsSchema is extended to include CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE in its schema map, making it likely that getResourceTypeResource returns (or creates) a non-null type resource for supported types. Therefore the claim that a null resource will be passed and cause an NPE/500 is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientRemovedEvent listener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 implements by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, causing client deletion to fail with a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` triggers `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This diff adds `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is implemented to always throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). If the V2 management path is used under this feature flag (as implied by the new V2 classes), client deletion would hit this listener and fail with a runtime exception (500).

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a permission decision, surfacing as a 500 rather than 403 or proper not-supported response

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` and explicitly overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` (and related permission methods) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any code path in the admin/token-exchange flow calls these evaluator methods while running under V2 (which is plausible because they are part of the permissions implementation), this will raise an unchecked exception rather than returning a permission decision (e.g., `false`) or a controlled HTTP error, which would typically surface as a 500 unless specifically mapped/caught. The diff shows no handling around these throws in `ClientPermissionsV2` itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource, creating an N+1 evaluation loop on the admin client-list path

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates all resources of type `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`, which performs `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))`. This is a per-resource policy evaluation inside a full scan loop (an N+1-style pattern) and is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff. The diff alone doesn’t prove it is definitely on the “admin client-list path”, but the method itself does create the described evaluation-per-resource behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient accepting both internal id and clientId creates a cross-namespace collision where a permission granted for client A can silently authorize client B

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(KeycloakSession, String) that resolves an identifier by first trying getClientById(realm, id) and then getClientByClientId(realm, id), returning the resolved client's internal ID. Because the same unqualified string can be interpreted as either an internal client UUID or a clientId, this creates an ambiguity/collision: if some client’s clientId happens to equal another client’s internal ID, a permission created targeting that string will be bound to the wrong client (whichever matches by internal ID first). That can silently authorize a different client than intended when permissions are created/evaluated based on this resolution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission passes a possibly null type-level resource to findByResource, producing an NPE or empty-policy 500 rather than a clean deny

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when the per-client resource is missing it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and then immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later constructs `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` without any null-check on `resource`. The diff does not show whether `getResourceTypeResource` is guaranteed to always return a non-null “type-level” resource (e.g., create-on-demand). If it can return null, this would cause an NPE/500 instead of a clean deny; if it cannot, the finding is moot. From the diff alone, the lack of a defensive null-check is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case concern but the claimed failure mode is not fully verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canView/canManageClientScopes/canManage collapse all client-scope decisions to the realm-wide all-clients resource, silently changing per-object semantics with no versioning or interface contract update
matched_golden_ids: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: client-specific permission checks end up using the realm-wide "all-clients" resource, effectively ignoring per-client permissions. The golden comment explains the root cause (resource lookup mismatch causing fallback), while the candidate describes the behavioral consequence (collapse of per-object decisions to all-clients).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the V1 client-deletion cleanup contract that AdminPermissions.registerListener depends on — client removal fails or orphans authz resources in V2 realms

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` triggers `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This PR adds `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), but `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). If `management(...)` resolves to `MgmtPermissionsV2` in the V2 path, client removal will throw at event handling time, preventing cleanup and potentially leaving orphaned authz data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange authorization in V2 realms (500 errors instead of grant/deny decisions)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds `ClientPermissionsV2` where `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and several other permission-building methods) are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is changed to return this new implementation, any code path in V2 that calls these methods would now fail at runtime rather than returning an allow/deny decision. However, the diff does not show token-exchange actually invoking these methods, so the claim about producing 500s and “breaking token-exchange authorization” cannot be fully verified from the diff alone; it is nonetheless a concrete, diff-grounded incompleteness risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, resource, getPermissions, and isPermissionsEnabled — breaking the admin console per-client Permissions tab and AdminPermissionsEvaluator REST API

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds ClientPermissionsV2 and wires it into MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() (MgmtPermissionsV2 now returns new ClientPermissionsV2). ClientPermissionsV2 overrides multiple methods (managePermission/configurePermission/viewPermission/mapRoles*Permission, resource, getPermissions, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled) to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). This is a concrete, diff-grounded incompleteness/compatibility concern: any existing code path in V2 mode that expects these operations will now fail at runtime. However, the finding’s specific claim that this "breaks the admin console per-client Permissions tab and AdminPermissionsEvaluator REST API" is not directly verifiable from the diff because no call sites/endpoints are shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which may disable role/group/client removal cleanup in V2 realms if governed by a different feature flag, causing orphaned authz resource accumulation
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup is incorrectly gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), which can prevent cleanup in V2 contexts governed by a different flag, leading to orphaned authorization data. This is the same underlying inconsistency and orphaned-permissions bug described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel) overrides V1 semantics of MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role with 'role OR realm-wide Clients MANAGE permission', silently granting client-scope management to a different population than documented

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly documents the V2 semantic expansion for client/client-scope operations: `ClientPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc for `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` and `canManageClientScopes()` states “For V2 only: Also if it has permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE`.” The V2 implementation matches this (`ClientPermissionsV2.canManage(ClientScopeModel)` delegates to `canManageClientScopes()`, which returns `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role OR `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). Therefore it is not “silently” granting to an undocumented population per the diff; it is documented in the interface comments added in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients fallback gate in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) tests the wrong permission population: findByResource misses resourceType-scoped permissions, so an all-clients grant fails per-client enforcement and admins get inconsistent 403s

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when the per-client Resource is missing it explicitly loads the resource-type (“all-clients”) Resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) before evaluating. The diff also adds tests (e.g., PermissionClientTest#testManageAllClients) that create an all-clients scope permission (resourceType=Clients, scopes={MANAGE}) and then perform per-client operations like deleting a specific client, which would rely on this fallback path if no per-client resource exists. That strongly indicates the fallback does not “miss” resourceType-scoped permissions in the way the finding claims, at least as implemented/used in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 overrides canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role short-circuit that V1 applies, denying role mapping to admins with the manage-clients role

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles to only call hasPermission(...), with no MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role short-circuit. However, the claim that this "drops" a V1 short-circuit cannot be verified from this diff because the V1 (ClientPermissions) implementations are not shown. Also, the updated interface Javadoc for these map-roles methods does not state that MANAGE_CLIENTS should grant them (unlike canManage/canView, which explicitly mention AdminRoles), suggesting this may be intentional rather than a regression proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-client policy-management methods (mapRolesPermission, managePermission, setPermissionsEnabled, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, so a MANAGE-scoped admin has no bootstrapping path to create the permission that would unblock themselves, causing 500s

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` where multiple methods, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)`, unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is updated to return this new `ClientPermissionsV2` implementation. In the same PR, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (now guarded by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`) handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);`. If `management(...)` resolves to `MgmtPermissionsV2` in this mode (consistent with the new V2 wiring), this will now throw at runtime, leading to a 500/error path during client removal cleanup. The finding’s broader "bootstrapping path" claim isn’t directly proven by the diff, but the UnsupportedOperationException causing runtime failures is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature-flag guard on event cleanup listeners is not the same switch that selects MgmtPermissionsV2, so if V2 is enabled while that flag is off, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers never run, accumulating orphaned Client resources and policies that leak deleted-client UUIDs and grow unboundedly

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a new guard in AdminPermissions.registerListener(): all cleanup handling for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent now runs only when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. However, the finding’s core claim—that MgmtPermissionsV2 can be selected/enabled by a different switch such that V2 runs while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is off—cannot be verified from this diff because the code that selects MgmtPermissionsV2 is not shown here. Without evidence in the diff that V2 can operate with the feature flag off, the asserted orphaned-resource leak scenario is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope in ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles has zero test coverage; the role-mapping test never imports or grants the scope, so the permission branch could regress unchecked

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` via `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the added/modified tests, `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient()` grants `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)` to the client, but never grants or exercises `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, and no other shown test references that scope. So the new permission branch is not covered by tests and could regress without detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Positive-path assertions in PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient are 'doesn't throw' checks with no state verification (e.g. no listAll() confirming role assignment)

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`, the post-permission “success” path only calls the admin endpoints (e.g., `users().get(...).roles().clientLevel(...).add(...)` and `roles().get(...).addComposites(...)`) without any follow-up assertion that the role mapping/composite relationship actually exists (no subsequent `listAll()`/`getComposites()`/representation fetch to verify state). This is a concrete test robustness gap introduced in the diff, but it’s not a product/runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients passes a null representation to create() when asserting 403, so it doesn't verify authorization denial for a valid client

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testViewAllClients`, the test attempts to verify that a user with only `VIEW` permission cannot create a client, but it calls `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(null)` and asserts `403` (Forbidden). Passing `null` is not a valid `ClientRepresentation`, so the request may fail for validation/Bad Request reasons instead of authorization, meaning the test does not reliably prove an authorization denial for a valid create operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener fails and per-client authorization Resource/scope-permission/policy rows are orphaned on client deletion under the V2 feature, potentially aborting client removal itself

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` triggers `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. The diff adds `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Therefore, under the V2 path this listener will throw during client removal cleanup, which can prevent the intended permission cleanup and may disrupt the removal flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions now wraps the entire role/client/group removal cleanup in a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check, so when the feature is disabled, previously-removed entities' permission resources are not cleaned up, leaving dangling rows that persist across disable-to-enable transitions

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener(...)`, the cleanup logic that reacts to `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` was previously unconditional, but is now entirely wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. As a result, when the feature is disabled these removal events no longer call `...setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which (by intent of this listener) is the mechanism to disable/cleanup fine-grained admin permission data for deleted entities. Skipping it can leave authorization resources/policies behind for entities that were removed while the feature was off, potentially causing dangling/stale rows that persist if the feature is later enabled again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveClient/getOrCreateResource uses client ID or clientId as resource name in the same name column, creating ambiguity where a clientId string matching another client's UUID-shaped name, or a re-created client with a new internal ID, causes lookups to miss the per-client resource and fall through to the all-clients resource or silently lose permissions, with no migration handling re-created clients

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `resolveClient()` always returns `client.getId()` (the internal UUID) even when the input is a `clientId` (`getClientByClientId` is only used to *find* the client, not to name the resource). `getOrCreateResource()` then uses that resolved value as the resource name. Likewise, `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` looks up resources by `client.getId()`. So the diff does not show resources being stored under either `clientId` or UUID “in the same name column”, nor a per-client resource being created under `clientId` such that it would later “fall through” to all-clients. The concern about recreated clients losing permissions is a broader design/migration issue not evidenced as a specific ambiguity introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException when called from AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent branch in V2 mode, causing client deletion to fail with a 500 and orphaned authz resources/policies

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). This diff introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException. If V2 management is used under this feature (as implied by the new V2 classes), a client removal event will trigger this exception, causing deletion to fail and skipping cleanup logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false, causing a 500 instead of a denied (403) decision during token-exchange authorization in V2 realms

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canExchangeTo(ClientModel authorizedClient, ClientModel to, AccessToken token)` is overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (see `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). Since this method’s contract is boolean authorization evaluation (deny/allow), throwing here would propagate as an unhandled runtime exception if the token-exchange path invokes it, resulting in a server error rather than a normal denied decision.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission NPEs when getResourceTypeResource returns null for the type-level all-clients resource, crashing canManage/canView on freshly-configured realms
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a NullPointerException in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission caused by getResourceTypeResource returning null, which aligns with the golden issue about needing defensive null checks before calling findByResource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasGrantedPermission re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() without a null guard, risking NPE for future callers since the null check lives in the calling method getClientsWithPermission

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) re-calls root.realmResourceServer() and does not null-check the result before passing it into new ResourcePermission(..., server) and root.evaluatePermission(..., server). However, in the current diff this private helper is only invoked from getClientsWithPermission(), which already returns early if server == null, so there is no verifiable NPE on the shown call path. The concern is primarily about robustness/maintainability (future internal callers or behavior changes), not a demonstrated defect in this diff.
